MUQATIL:10:45-46/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:45-46/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:45-46/r1.claim: When resurrected from their graves, people will think they remained only one day and will recognize one another; Muqatil links this to 70:1 and 70:11.

MUQATIL:10:45-46/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:45-46/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:45-46/r2.claim: Those who denied meeting God denied resurrection and have lost the way.

TAB-FULL:v12p187#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p187#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p187#2/r1.claim: At the gathering for judgment, the disbelievers will seem to have lived only an hour and briefly recognize one another before that recognition ends.

TAB-FULL:v12p187#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p187#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p187#2/r2.claim: Those denying God's meeting lose their share of good, denying both divine reward and punishment and bringing ruin upon themselves.

TAB-FULL:v12p187#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p187#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p187#2/r3.claim: Their lack of guidance means they were not directed to sound judgment in denying God's meeting, which earned them a punishment they cannot withstand.

ZAJJAJ:v3p22/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p22/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p22/r1.claim: The interval between death and resurrection will seem short, as in the report ‘we remained a day or part of a day.’

ZAJJAJ:v3p22/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p22/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p22/r2.claim: Their recognizing one another exposes their mutual misguidance, rebukes them, and establishes the proof against them.

ZAJJAJ:v3p22/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p22/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p22/r3.claim: ‘Those who denied meeting God have lost’ may be God’s declaration after the proof of resurrection, or words the people say as they recognize one another.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1954#6/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1954#6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1954#6/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the gathering period as death.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1954#6/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1954#6/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1954#6/r2.claim: Hasan says people recognize the companion beside them on Judgment Day but do not speak to him.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1954#6/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1954#6/r3.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1954#6/r3.claim: Abu Razin says those who denied meeting God had already gone astray.

NAHHAS:v2p257/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p257/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p257/r1.claim: يتعارفون is circumstantial; the loss statement may be God's report or their words while recognizing one another.

THALABI:v5p134/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p134/r2.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v5p134/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the gathered people will feel they remained in worldly life only an hour because its duration shrinks before the terrors ahead.

THALABI:v5p134/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p134/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p134/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says they seem to have stayed in their graves an hour; on resurrection they recognize one another as in life, then recognition ends when they see the terrors.

THALABI:v5p134/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p134/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p134/r4.claim: Those who denied meeting God have lost and were not guided.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p436#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p436#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p436#2/r1.claim: The short stay of a daytime hour may refer to life in the world or to the grave, which feels brief because of its nearness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p436#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p436#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p436#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says people recognize one another when they emerge from their graves, but recognition then ceases.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p436#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p436#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p436#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that they recognize that what they followed was false.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r1.claim: Ka-anna is the lightened form of the emphatic particle, with an omitted pronoun understood as ka-annahum; two poetic lines illustrate the construction.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people seem to have stayed in their graves for only an hour of the day.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the interval between death and resurrection seems brief, as in 23:113.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn al-Anbari say the time between death and resurrection feels like an hour because of the terror of resurrection and Judgment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p209#2/r5.claim: Another view takes their brief stay as the duration of worldly life, not their time in the intermediate state.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil say people recognize each other when raised from their graves as they did in life, then recognition ends.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says recognition and awareness of who misled whom reproach them and establish proof against them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says their recognition is mutual accusation—'you led me astray'—not compassion; this fits 70:10 as a denial of merciful concern, while exegetes assign the two verses to different stages.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r4.claim: Abu Ali offers two readings of yataʿārafūn: they discover how long they stayed, with the object omitted, or they recognize one another; the latter fits the exchanges in 37:50–51 and 52:26.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p211/r5.claim: Abu Ali gives three syntactic parses for 'as though they had stayed': an adjective of the day with 'before it' omitted, an adjective of the verbal noun, or a circumstantial phrase attached to the object of 'We gather'.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p214/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p214/r1.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p214/r1.claim: The second parse makes the phrase an adjective of the verbal noun 'gathering', with 'before it' omitted; the third makes it a state of the object, as if their condition were that of one who stayed only an hour.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p214/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p214/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p214/r2.claim: Yawm may be governed by yataʿārafūn as a time adverb or metaphorically as an object, like 'thief of the night the people of the house'; alternatively it may be governed by the meaning of ka-an lam yalbathū.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p214/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p214/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p214/r3.claim: Abu Ali calls the last syntactic option weak: whichever parse is chosen, the adjective cannot govern its noun or an already annexed day without violating Arabic word order and attachment rules.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r1.claim: The commentators say those who denied resurrection lost the reward of Paradise.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari links their loss to the preceding recognition: after describing resurrection and the resurrected, the verse states the loss of its deniers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq reads the statement as explaining, after establishing resurrection, that whoever denies it has lost.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p215/r4.claim: Abu Bakr offers another reading: they are already lost during the mutual recognition, when repentance and reprieve are no longer possible.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:45-47/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:45-47/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:45-47/r1.claim: At the gathering, people will think they remained in their graves only an hour of a day because the terror of resurrection makes the time seem brief.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:45-47/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:45-47/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:45-47/r2.claim: They recognize one another in mutual reproach, each blaming the other for leading them astray.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:45-47/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:45-47/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:45-47/r3.claim: Those who deny meeting God have lost the reward of Paradise by denying resurrection.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r2.speaker: حفص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r2.claim: Hafs reads the verb for gathering with ياء; the other readers use نون.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the people will seem to have remained in worldly life only an hour of a day.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says they will seem to have remained in their graves only an hour of a day.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r5.claim: They recognize one another when raised as they did in worldly life, but recognition ends when they witness the terrors of resurrection.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r6.claim: An account says a person will know who stands beside him on Judgment Day but will not speak from awe and fear.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p135#2/r7.claim: The loss is the loss of one’s own soul, the greatest possible loss.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r4.claim: The gathering is a threat of humiliation and mutual reproach; يوم may be governed by an omitted اذكر, by the verb implied in كأن لم يلبثوا, or by يتعارفون.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r5.claim: The comparison with a daytime hour can modify the day, serve as an absolute accusative, or be circumstantial; daytime is specified because its familiar divisions make the shortness of their stay vivid.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r6.claim: يتعارفون may describe mutual recognition and reproach at Resurrection, or be circumstantial from the gathering; alternatively it describes recognition in worldly life, whose ties will seem no longer than an hour at Resurrection, as al-Tabari explains.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r7.speaker: السبعة وجمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r7.claim: They read نحشرهم with nūn; a report from al-A'mash has يحشرهم with yāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p122#3/r8.claim: The verdict calls deniers losers and exposes their delusion about God; the words may be God's report or the gathered people's self-reproach.

TABRISI:10:45#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45#2/r1.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45#2/r1.claim: The phrase يوم نحشرهم may be governed by يتعارفون or by the meaning implied in كأن لم يلبثوا.

TABRISI:10:45#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45#2/r2.claim: If يتعارفون governs the day, يوم can be an adverb meaning they recognize one another on that day, or an object by broad syntactic extension.

TABRISI:10:45#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45#2/r3.claim: On the first analysis, recognition concerns their period of death before resurrection, with its object omitted; alternatively, يتعارفون implies other verbs that govern knowing their period of stay.

TABRISI:10:45#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45#2/r4.claim: The day can instead be governed by the meaning that their condition resembled that of people who had not stayed long, even with that meaning preceding the time expression.

TABRISI:10:45#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45#2/r5.claim: That construction cannot make يوم a description of the verbal noun or of the day itself, since the described noun follows the verb and an adjective cannot govern its noun.

TABRISI:10:45#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45#2/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45#2/r6.claim: Nor can the construction be a circumstantial description governed through a genitive day, because that would require the dependent to precede its governing noun.

TABRISI:10:45#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:45#2/r7.claim: The nūn reading is supported by other Qur'anic uses of gathering in the first-person plural.

TABRISI:10:45#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45#2/r8.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45#2/r8.claim: A second cited passage illustrates mutual recognition through people asking one another how long they stayed.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:45-47/r1.claim: God gathers them from every place to the assembly ground, where they seem to have remained in the world only an hour of a day.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:45-47/r10.claim: They lose worldly life by spending it in sins and forfeit the bliss of the hereafter through those sins.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r2.speaker: الضحاك وجماعة
TABRISI:10:45-47/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak and others say they regard worldly days as brief because even a long worldly stay is like an hour beside the hereafter.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:45-47/r3.claim: Another view says their stay seemed short because they gained little from their lives through their poor use of them.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:10:45-47/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says they regarded their time in the graves as brief.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:45-47/r5.claim: The image warns people not to be deceived by hopes of long worldly survival, since it ends in passing away.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:45-47/r6.claim: People recognize one another at that time as they did in worldly life.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r7.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:10:45-47/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says they recognize one another's former error and disbelief on leaving their graves, then recognition ends when they see punishment and they disavow one another.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:10:45-47/r8.claim: Meeting God here means meeting God's recompense; the losers were not guided to the truth.

TABRISI:10:45-47/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45-47/r9.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:10:45-47/r9.claim: Hasan says they lost themselves because they were not guided in worldly life; had they been guided, they would not have lost themselves.

TABRISI:10:45/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45/r1.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
TABRISI:10:45/r1.claim: Hafs, transmitting from Asim, reads ويوم يحشرهم with yā; the other readers use nūn.

TABRISI:10:45/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45/r2.claim: Abu Ali says كأن لم يلبثوا may be an adjective of يوم, an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, or a circumstantial clause describing the object pronoun.

TABRISI:10:45/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45/r3.claim: If it modifies يوم, one interpretation is that they had stayed only an hour before that day, with قبله omitted, as in the cited constructions.

TABRISI:10:45/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45/r4.claim: A second analysis omits a genitive noun before the adjective, lets the genitive stand in its place, then omits the adjective's pronoun, as in the cited phrase.

TABRISI:10:45/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45/r5.claim: If the clause modifies an omitted verbal noun, it follows the same analysis as the preceding interpretation.

TABRISI:10:45/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:10:45/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:10:45/r6.claim: If it is a circumstantial clause for the object pronoun, nothing need be omitted: their state at gathering resembles that of people who stayed only an hour.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r1.claim: The brief worldly life is insignificant beside the harm of the disbelievers' severe punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r2.claim: Mutual recognition can mean they know one another as in worldly life, or identify each other's former misguidance and then disown one another at the sight of punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r3.claim: The recognition does not conflict with 70:10: either it is mutual reproach rather than a compassionate request for help, or recognition occurs at resurrection and then ceases.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r4.claim: قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله may continue the gathered people's speech, or be God's own testimony that whoever traded the lasting hereafter for worldly life lost.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84#2/r5.claim: They were not guided to protect their interests in this trade: they mistook the world's attractive appearance for true value, like buying glass as a jewel.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r1.claim: The warning follows the disbelievers' failure to listen and reflect.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r10.claim: The author argues that enduring, humiliating pain overwhelms limited, mixed worldly pleasures, making earthly life negligible beside eternal punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r2.claim: Hafs from ʿĀṣim reads يحشرهم with yāʾ; the other readers use نون.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r3.claim: The phrase كأن لم يلبثوا is circumstantial, while يتعارفون can modify the day of gathering or form another circumstantial clause.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r4.claim: The source analyzes كان as a lightened form of the emphatic particle, with an implied pronoun, as in the expression وكأن قد.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r5.claim: Some say the short stay was in their graves; others say it was their earthly life, a distinction also reflected in 23:112–113.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r6.claim: The Qāḍī prefers that they regard worldly life as brief: believers too cannot measure the postmortem interval, but disbelievers wasted their lives, and mutual recognition belongs to life rather than the grave.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r7.claim: Abū Muslim says they saw their wasted pursuit of worldly pleasure as having yielded nothing, so their lifespan seemed like nonexistence.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r8.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r8.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the afterlife's terrors made their earthly stay seem short, since intense fear makes other things slip from awareness.

RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p84/r9.claim: Other explanations compare worldly life with the everlasting afterlife or long assembly, or say death seemed brief because people recognized one another again on leaving the graves.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r1.claim: The phrase ‘as though they had not stayed’ abbreviates ‘as though they had not stayed in their graves’; the resurrection’s terror makes the grave seem as short as an hour.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r10.claim: ‘They were not guided’ means they were not among those God knew to be guided.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says people view their whole earthly lifetimes as an hour when compared with eternity.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r3.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says people recognize one another as they did in life after leaving the graves; their recognition is reproach and exposure, not compassion.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r4.claim: One view says recognition ends at the sight of Judgment’s terrors, while Qurtubi prefers the view that reproach continues, supported by scenes of mutual cursing and blaming leaders.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r5.claim: ‘No close friend asks another’ and ‘no kinship among them’ mean no question prompted by mercy or sympathy, not that recognition and blame cease altogether.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r6.claim: Other views say resurrection has different locations, or that recognition means asking each other how long they stayed; Qurtubi calls the latter a good interpretation.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r7.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says believers recognize one another with affection, while unbelievers receive no mutual affection.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r8.claim: Those who denied meeting God lost the reward of Paradise, either as a declaration after proof of resurrection or at the actual encounter where reprieve and repentance no longer help.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r9.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:10:45/r9.claim: Al-Nahhas says ‘they recognize one another’ could be the disbelievers saying that they have lost.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r1.claim: On resurrection, people will think their stay in the world or graves lasted only an hour because of the terror they witness.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r2.claim: The comparison clause may be circumstantial, an adjective of the Day, or describe an omitted source noun; its omitted referent may be the time before resurrection.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r3.claim: They first recognize one another as if they had been apart only briefly, but recognition later ceases because events overwhelm them; alternatively this phrase explains their short estimate of time.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r4.claim: The statement that those who denied meeting God lost is either a fresh testimony to their loss or a circumstantial clause expressing their speech.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:45/r5.claim: They were not guided in using their faculties to gain knowledge; instead, they acquired ignorance that led to ruin and lasting punishment.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r1.claim: At resurrection they think their worldly life or time in graves lasted only an hour; they recognize one another on emerging, then recognition ceases as the ordeal intensifies.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r2.speaker: حفص
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r2.claim: Hafs reads the verb for gathering with yāʾ.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r3.claim: The form is a shortened kāna with omitted name; recognition can be a circumstantial clause or an independent statement.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r4.claim: Their loss can be spoken by them or be God's testimony; they spent faith as capital and traded it for disbelief, without knowing the trade.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p130#6/r5.claim: The closing statement is an independent expression of astonishment at how great their loss is.

QASHANI:10:45/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:10:45/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:10:45/r1.claim: People think an hour or ages have passed equally because not sensing motion makes them unaware of time.

QASHANI:10:45/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:10:45/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:10:45/r2.claim: Recognition persists through prior companionship and innate affinity when people share an orientation; differing desires and material traits turn recognition into estrangement.

QASHANI:10:45/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:10:45/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:10:45/r3.claim: Those denying encounter with God lose innate light and become estranged behind corrupt habits and beliefs, unable to find God or recognize one another, friendless and rejected.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r1.claim: He parses كأن لم يلبثوا as a state of the resurrected; يتعارفون either modifies the time as a circumstance or explains that recognition persists for a while before turning into mutual denial.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r2.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥawfi parses يتعارفون as a circumstantial future participle from يلبثوا or as a circumstance of نحشرهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r3.claim: The proposed source-noun parse requires an omitted قبله to link the comparison to the noun, but Abū Ḥayyān says deleting this connector is impermissible.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r4.claim: Other parsers allow يتعارفون to be a circumstantial clause, or an independent report that recognition occurs between them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says they recognize each other as they did in life when leaving their graves, but the recognition is blame and exposure rather than affection, then ends amid the terrors of resurrection.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r6.claim: One view says they recognize one another's former error and disbelief.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets recognition as the believers showing mutual affection, while unbelievers have no family ties among them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r8.claim: Another view says resurrection has different stations: people recognize each other in some and not in others.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64#2/r9.claim: The declaration that the deniers lost is apparently an independent report; Zamakhshari calls it an exclamation or a statement spoken during their recognition.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r1.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ḥafṣ read يحشرهم with yāʾ, making God the unspoken subject in continuity with the preceding mention of God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r2.claim: The resurrected will feel their worldly life or time in the graves lasted only briefly, either because of the terrors they see or the long day and its accounting.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they view their long lifetimes as an hour when compared with eternity.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers several parses for يوم: an implicit command to remember, an implied verb of swiftness, or the verb يتعارفون; he also suggests the comparison may modify the day, a source noun, or the object pronoun.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān finds Ibn ʿAṭiyya's implied swiftness analysis unexplained, and rejects making the comparison an adjective of the definite day: the clause describes the resurrected, not the day.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p64/r6.claim: The apparent syntax makes كأن لم يلبثوا a circumstantial clause attached to the object pronoun of نحشرهم, as Zamakhshari and Abu al-Baqa also parse it.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية وأبو البقاء ومكي
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r1.claim: They parse كأن لم يلبثوا as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, تقديره يحشرهم حشرات كأن لم يلبثوا; some also posit an omitted pronoun linking it.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the clause an elliptical statement but does not identify its implied verb.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r3.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r3.claim: Al-Hawfi's proposed implicit meaning is speed: they hasten as though they had stayed only an hour.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#2/r4.claim: On that reading يسرعون is circumstantial from the object of يحشرهم, and كأن لم may describe its subject or explain the implied hastening.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r1.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r1.claim: Al-Hawfi parses يتعارفون as a circumstantial clause from the subject of يلبثوا: they are gathered while recognizing one another.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r2.claim: Another parse makes يتعارفون circumstantial from the object of يحشرهم; Abu al-Baqa calls it an estimated state because recognition does not occur during the act of gathering.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows يتعارفون to attach circumstantially to the time adverb or to explain the brief stay: long separation erases recognition and turns it into estrangement.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#3/r4.claim: يتعارفون may instead be an independent statement about them.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r1.claim: قد خسر may be an independent emphatic report that those who deny meeting God are certainly losers.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes قد خسر as an independent exclamatory statement or as an implied saying by those recognizing one another.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats the implied saying قد خسر as a circumstantial clause from the object of يحشرهم.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:45#4/r4.claim: وما كانوا مهتدين either coordinates with قد خسر or is part of the relative clause of الذين, reinforcing that those who deny God’s meeting are unguided.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r1.claim: ويوم is a time adverb governed by the verb implied in كأن لم يلبثوا, by يتعارفون, or by an omitted اذكر.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r2.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads يحشرهم with third-person yā; the pronoun refers to God, named in the preceding verse.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats كأن لم يلبثوا as an adjective of يوم.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r4.claim: Al-Shaykh rejects that adjective parse because يوم يحشرهم is definite, the clause is indefinite, and semantically the clause describes the gathered people rather than their day.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r5.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r5.claim: Makki tries to supply قبله as a deleted link, making the clause mean they had not remained before that day; the author says deleting this link is invalid.

SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r6.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية ومكي وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:10:45/r6.claim: They allow كأن لم يلبثوا as a circumstantial clause from the object of يحشرهم, meaning they are gathered as though they had remained only an hour.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p271#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p271#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p271#2/r1.claim: People will recognize children, parents, and relatives as in worldly life, though each will be preoccupied; kinship will not prompt mutual concern.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p271#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p271#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p271#2/r2.claim: Those who denied meeting God lose themselves and their families through separation from beloved ones on the Day of Regret, the greatest loss.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p271/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p271/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p271/r1.claim: At resurrection, people gathered from their graves will feel that they lived in this world only a brief part of a day; this demonstrates the world's brevity relative to the Hereafter.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p447#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p447#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p447#2/r4.claim: People who deny resurrection live as though time were ample and danger remote, but on gathering their worldly stay seems only a small daytime hour.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p447#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p447#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p447#2/r5.claim: Their brief stay gains them only mutual recognition, increasing regret because they cannot support or help one another as they did in worldly life.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p447#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p447#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p447#2/r6.claim: Those who denied meeting God truly lost by taking transient lowly goods over enduring noble reward; the explicit label generalizes the judgment, and their failure to be guided was habitual.

BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r1.claim: The gathered pious are brought before the Merciful as honored guests; people recognize each other as in worldly life, as if death were only a brief separation.

BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r2.claim: Recognition later stops when they see punishment, and they disown one another; the verse declares and marvels at the loss of those denying meeting God.

BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r3.claim: They were cheated in their trade, exchanging faith for unbelief and truth for denial, with no benefit left once time had passed.

BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p24#2/r4.claim: A Persian saying has a teacher tell a child that they did no work and the day has passed, warning against wasting life.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r1.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads يحشرهم with yāʾ; the other readers use the first-person plural, shifting to direct address.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r10.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r10.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls recognition a prospective circumstantial clause, but al-Ālūsī sees no need to suppose a delay after resurrection.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r11.claim: Recognition occurs on first emerging from the graves, then may cease amid terror; al-Ālūsī adds that different scenes could allow renewed recognition after estrangement.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r12.claim: Some commentators allege a conflict between recognition and verses denying kinship and mutual questioning.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r2.claim: Most grammarians take يوم as an object of an omitted command to remember or warn them of the day of gathering for judgment.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r3.claim: The hour of a day is proverbial for an extremely short time; daytime is specified because its hours are more familiar than nighttime hours.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r4.claim: The simile is a circumstantial description of the gathered people, as if their stay in worldly life or the barzakh had been only brief.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r5.claim: The comparison chiefly expresses regret at wasting their lives or wishing they had remained longer before witnessing the terrors; reading it literally is less persuasive.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r6.claim: Some preserve the literal comparison by saying long-lived people would retain signs of worldly prosperity, but al-Ālūsī calls this an artificial reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r7.claim: If the brief stay refers to the barzakh, it can show resurrection's ease despite its duration and answer their denial, or indicate that forms remain unchanged after a short interval.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r8.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r8.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows the clause to describe the Day or an omitted noun for resurrection, but objections concern its deleted link and definiteness; al-Ālūsī favors the circumstantial reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p127#2/r9.claim: The clause about mutual recognition either resumes the account or explains the brief-stay comparison; the inference from recognition to short duration is not conclusive.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r1.claim: The statement that the deniers lost is best read as God's independent testimony to their loss, though some make it quoted speech or a circumstantial clause.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r2.claim: The wording identifies them as those who denied meeting God to condemn them by the trait that caused their fate; meeting means reckoning and recompense, and loss is failed spiritual commerce.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r3.claim: An alternative takes meeting as a bad encounter and loss as ruin and misguidance.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r4.claim: They were not guided either in the figurative trade of salvation or toward the road to safety; the final clause coordinates with the loss statement or reinforces the relative clause.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a person recognizes the neighbor beside him but cannot speak to him.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p128/r6.claim: Taking recognition to mean that people identify one another's past error and disbelief is an unsupported interpretation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r1.claim: The account returns to resurrection after discussing idolatry and the Quran; the judgment day exposes both false gods and deniers of resurrection, completing a ring structure.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r2.claim: يوم is an adverb attached to خسروا: they lose on the day of resurrection; fronting it emphasizes warning and proof of that day's reality.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r3.claim: Calling them 'those who denied meeting God' instead of using a pronoun identifies denial as the cause of loss and links it to the preceding account of shirk.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r4.claim: Most readers use first-person plural نحشرهم; Hafs reads third-person يحشرهم, with the pronoun returning to God's name in 10:44.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p181#3/r5.claim: The short-stay comparison is either parenthetical between gathering and recognition or a circumstantial clause describing those gathered.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r1.claim: كأن is the softened form of كأنّ; its usually omitted subject is estimated as هم from the preceding pronouns.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r2.claim: The image compares people gathered after long periods in graves to themselves if they had stayed only a daytime hour.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r3.claim: من is partitive but not restrictive: day is the familiar reference for a short time, as in the conventional use of رجال and the hadith about an hour of a day.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r4.claim: An hour means a span of time, usually a short one, as in the discussion of 7:34.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r5.claim: The comparison stresses that elapsed time does not prevent resurrection and that people return with their identities; this displays God's power.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r6.claim: The short stay rebuts the polytheists' claim that long burial and bodily change make resurrection impossible, raised in 79:10–11.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p182/r7.claim: يتعارفون بينهم is a circumstantial clause: each recognizes the others whom he knew in worldly life.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p183/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p183/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p183/r1.claim: Mutual recognition, like the short-stay comparison, shows that they are gathered with their worldly bodies and faculties, further refuting the claim that death destroys resurrection's possibility.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p183/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p183/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p183/r2.claim: Their loss becomes clear because they denied resurrection and failed to prepare by accepting the Messenger's call.

TABATABAI:10:45/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:45/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:45/r1.claim: He parses the phrase about their short stay as a circumstantial clause describing them as they are gathered.

TABATABAI:10:45/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:45/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:45/r2.claim: He calls the alternatives that the brief-lifetime phrase modifies the day or deleted verbal noun, and that recognition modifies the hour, remote and unsupported by the wording.

TABATABAI:10:45/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:45/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:45/r3.claim: The deniers lose when gathered because they see worldly life as only an hour and recognize one another without forgetting or denying each other.

TABATABAI:10:45/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:45/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:45/r4.claim: The passage returns to the surah’s opening theme of meeting God: the future unveiling of religion will expose worldly life’s brevity and the ultimate sovereignty of the One.

ASAD-NOTES:10:45#n65/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:45#n65/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:45#n65/r1.claim: Earthly life will seem momentary beside the timeless afterlife, and earthly relationships will have been severed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: On the Day of Judgment, each soul would ransom itself with all worldly treasure if possible, showing why deniers should not call for doom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The promised punishment may arrive during the Prophet’s life or later, but a messenger’s nation is certainly judged in this world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: At resurrection people will think their worldly stay brief and recognize one another as if constantly meeting; memories remain fresh, so treating worldly life as lengthy makes them heedless of the hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: When warned about the hereafter, the deniers paradoxically demand its arrival.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:45/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:45/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:45/r1.claim: At the gathering, people will think worldly life—or, in a weaker view, their stay in the grave—lasted only an hour of a day; continued mutual recognition makes separation seem brief (compare 79:46).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:45/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:45/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:45/r2.claim: Later, worldly companions will be separated and each person will face either joy or grief according to faith and deeds (80:34–42); those who denied the meeting with God face the greatest loss.

QIRAAT-ER:10:45:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:10:45:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:10:45:3#1/r1.claim: The first-person plural shifts the divine voice from third person to the royal We.

STUDYQURAN:10:45/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:45/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:45/r1.claim: Disbelievers will see worldly life or the interval between death and resurrection as lasting only an hour of the day.

STUDYQURAN:10:45/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:45/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:45/r2.claim: Those who deny meeting God suffer loss as a consequence of that denial.
